results.name: Elevated Pike Shoulder Shrug
instructions: Place the balls of both feet on an elevated platform and position your hands shoulder width apart on the floor. Straighten your arms and legs, then lift your hips until your body forms an inverted V shape.
Keep your elbows fixed with a slight bend, lowering your upper body slightly between your arms.
Press firmly through your palms and shrug your shoulders upwards, raising your upper body without bending your elbows.
Lower your shoulders with control to return to the starting position, then repeat while keeping your feet fixed and your hips elevated.
tips: Keep your hands shoulder width apart and spread your fingers for stability.
Keep your elbows fixed with a slight bend so the movement occurs through your shoulder blades.
Keep your legs extended and the balls of your feet firmly supported on the platform.
Exhale as you shrug your shoulders upward and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Elevated Pike Shoulder Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core, Forearms.

results.name: EZ Bar Seated Close Grip Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, holding an EZ bar with a close overhand grip. Position the bar at shoulder height with your palms facing your neck and your elbows pointing forward.
Press the bar overhead by extending your elbows upward.
Fully extend your arms without locking your elbows at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back to the starting position at shoulder height with control, keeping your elbows pointing forward.
tips: Ensure your elbows stay in front of you throughout the movement to effectively target the shoulders.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top to keep tension on the shoulder muscles.
Inhale as you lower the bar and exhale as you press it overhead.
results.description: EZ Bar Seated Close Grip Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: EZ Bar Standing Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Let the bar hang in front of your thighs.
Raise the EZ bar directly in front of you to shoulder height until parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder muscles.
Lower the bar back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
tips: Avoid using momentum to lift the bar; focus on a controlled motion.
Exhale as you lift the bar and inhale as you lower it.
Keep your wrists in a neutral position to avoid strain.
results.description: EZ Bar Standing Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: EZ Barbell Anti Gravity Press
instructions: Lie chest first on an incline bench, holding an EZ barbell with palms facing the floor, hands positioned shoulder-width apart. Hold the barbell close to your shoulders, just under your face, with elbows bent.
Press the barbell forward in a straight line until your arms are fully extended, keeping the bar parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the end of the movement, ensuring your arms are straight and the barbell is fully extended forward.
Return the barbell back to the starting position with control, bringing it close to your shoulders. Repeat the exercise.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on a controlled and steady motion.
Exhale as you press the barbell forward and inhale as you lower it.
Focus on using your shoulders to press the weight, minimizing lower back involvement.
results.description: EZ Barbell Anti Gravity Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Front Raise Resistance Bands
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the resistance band under both feet. Hold the handles of the resistance band with your palms facing backwards and your arms extended down in front of you.
Raise your arms straight in front of you to shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain.
Stand with a slight bend in your knees for better stability.
results.description: Front Raise Resistance Bands is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Front Raise (Overhead)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing your hips), hands placed at shoulder-width.
Lift the barbell in front of you by raising your arms straight out until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold the barbell at the top of the movement for a brief moment, ensuring your shoulders are fully engaged.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner, keeping your arms straight throughout the movement.
tips: Avoid using momentum to lift the barbell; focus on using your shoulder muscles.
Keep your core engaged to prevent arching your lower back.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: Barbell Front Raise (Overhead) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Upper Back.

results.name: Handstand Push on Chair
instructions: Begin by placing a sturdy chair against a wall for stability. Position yourself in front of the chair, with your back facing it.
Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, about a foot away from the chair. Kick up into a handstand position, with your feet resting on the seat of the chair.
Slowly lower your head towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight and your core engaged.
Push through your hands to extend your arms and return to the starting handstand position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core throughout the exercise to maintain stability and prevent arching your back.
Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
results.description: Handstand Push on Chair is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Upper Back.

results.name: Incline Lateral Raises Dumbbell
instructions: Adjust an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie chest-first against it, with your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), allowing the dumbbells to hang down towards the floor in line with your shoulders.
Keeping your arms slightly bent at the elbows, raise the dumbbells up and out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to reduce joint strain.
Keep your body stabilized against the bench to isolate your shoulder muscles.
Use a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Incline Lateral Raises Dumbbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Alternate Arms
instructions: Sit on the Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press machine, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward.
Press one handle upward by extending your arm fully while keeping the other arm stationary.
Squeeze your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement and slowly return the handle to the starting position with control.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handle upward and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
results.description: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Alternate Arms is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Both Arms
instructions: Sit on the Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press machine, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward.
Press both handles upward by extending your arms fully with control.
Squeeze your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement and slowly return the handles to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handles upward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Both Arms is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.
